questions.question_english: Under Section 21 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, every establishment is statutorily mandated to notify and publish a formal document detailing its measures to provide a barrier-free, supportive, and non-discriminatory environment. What is this official document called?
options_english: Inclusive Employment Protocol
Equal Opportunity Policy
Barrier-Free Workplace Guideline

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 21(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, read with Rules 8 and 9 of the RPwD Rules, 2017, every establishment (including educational institutions, autonomous bodies, and government departments) is legally mandated to notify and publish an 'Equal Opportunity Policy' (EOP). This policy must detail the infrastructure, reasonable accommodations, barrier-free access, non-discriminatory recruitment, assistive technologies, and grievance redressal mechanisms provided to persons with disabilities. Furthermore, a copy of the Equal Opportunity Policy must be formally registered with the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (at the Central level) or the State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (at the State level). It also must be displayed prominently on the establishment's website or notice board.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the fundamentals of taxation for a salaried individual:
I. Total Income is calculated after allowing deductions under Chapter VI-A from the Gross Total Income.
II. Salary income is taxed on a due basis or receipt basis, whichever is earlier.
III. An individual is liable to pay Advance Tax if their estimated tax liability for the financial year is ₹10,000 or more.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
All three statements are correct under the Income Tax Act, 1961:
1. Statement I is correct: Total Income (taxable income) under Section 2(45) and Section 80A is derived by deducting allowable deductions under Chapter VI-A (Sections 80C, 80D, etc.) from the Gross Total Income (aggregate of all heads).
2. Statement II is correct: Under Section 15, income under the head 'Salaries' is chargeable to tax on a due basis (accrual) or receipt basis, whichever occurs earlier.
3. Statement III is correct: Under Section 208, advance tax is mandatory for any assessee whose estimated tax liability for the financial year (after accounting for TDS/TCS) is ₹10,000 or more.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 के अनुसार तीनों कथन सही हैं:
1. कथन I सही है: सकल कुल आय (GTI) में से अध्याय VI-A (धारा 80C से 80U) के तहत अनुमत कटौतियां घटाने के बाद ही कुल कर-योग्य आय (Total Income) प्राप्त होती है।
2. कथन II सही है: धारा 15 के अनुसार, वेतन आय देय होने की तिथि अथवा प्राप्त होने की तिथि, जो भी पहले घटित हो, पर कर-योग्य होती है।
3. कथन III सही है: धारा 208 के अंतर्गत, यदि किसी निर्धारिती की संबंधित वित्तीय वर्ष में टीडीएस कटौती के पश्चात शुद्ध कर देनदारी ₹10,000 या उससे अधिक बनती है, तो उसे अग्रिम कर (एडवांस टैक्स) देना अनिवार्य होता है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II, and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Total income is determined after subtracting Chapter VI-A deductions from gross total income. Income under salaries is taxable on due or receipt basis, whichever occurs earlier. Furthermore, advance tax provisions mandate that any individual whose estimated tax liability equals or exceeds ten thousand rupees in a financial year must pay tax in advance.

questions.question_english: Every Ministry, Department, and subordinate government establishment is required to appoint an officer to ensure strict compliance with reservation orders and roster maintenance. What is the official designation of this officer?
options_english: Reservation Supervisor
Affirmative Action Officer
Liaison Officer
Equity Commissioner
questions.explanation_english: Under Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) guidelines (OM No. 43011/153/2010-Estt.(Res) and related orders), each Ministry, Department, and attached/subordinate office is mandatorily required to designate a senior officer—at least of the rank of Deputy Secretary or Director/Joint Secretary—as a "Liaison Officer". The Liaison Officer is specifically responsible for ensuring strict compliance with reservation orders for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD). Under Section 9(1) of the POSH Act, 2013, the limitation period for filing a complaint is strictly codified as follows:
'Any aggrieved woman may make, in writing, a complaint of sexual harassment at workplace to the Internal Committee if so constituted, or the Local Committee, in case it is not so constituted, within a period of three months from the date of incident and in case of a series of incidents, within a period of three months from the date of last incident.'

Key Principles:
1. Isolated Incident: The complaint must be made within three months from the date of the occurrence.
2. Continuing Misconduct / Series of Incidents: Where an employee is subjected to ongoing harassment, the three-month period begins from the date of the last occurrence in that sequence.
3. Statutory Extension: The ICC may extend this period by another three months under the second proviso to Section 9(1) if sufficient cause prevented timely filing.

Thus, option (B) accurately states the limitation period.

questions.question_english: Under the POCSO Act, 2012, in the event of a dispute or uncertainty regarding the age of a person, how is the age of the child determined?
options_english: By physical appearance assessment conducted by the investigating police officer
By asking the child or immediate family members to verbally declare their age
According to procedures laid down under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
By an affidavit signed by the local village Sarpanch or municipal councillor
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 34(2) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, if any question arises in any proceeding before the Special Court whether a person is a child or not, the Special Court must determine the age of such person after satisfying itself and record reasons in writing. To resolve such disputes, the Special Court follows the age determination procedure statutorily codified under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act), as consistently affirmed by the Supreme Court of India (e.g., in Jarnail Singh v. State of Haryana). Under Section 94 of the JJ Act, the determination follows an exact statutory hierarchy of evidence: (1) Date of birth certificate from the school or the matriculation/equivalent certificate from the concerned examination board; (2) In the absence thereof, the birth certificate given by a corporation, municipal authority, or panchayat; (3) In the absence of both documentary proofs, age is determined through an ossification test or other latest medical age-determination test conducted by a duly constituted Medical Board. For school Principals, admission registers and transfer certificates maintained in official school custody constitute vital legal records during such inquiries.

विद्यालय प्राचार्य द्वारा संधारित छात्र प्रवेश रजिस्टर (Scholar Register) और जन्म प्रमाण पत्र इस प्रक्रिया में अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण साक्ष्य माने जाते हैं।

questions.question_english: Which of the following constitutional articles works in tandem with Article 15(4) to permit the reservation of seats for SC, ST, and SEBC candidates in educational institutions?
options_english: Article 29(2)
Article 19(1)(g)
Article 30(1)
Article 21
questions.explanation_english: Article 15(4) operates in direct conjunction with Article 29(2) of the Indian Constitution. Article 29(2) guarantees that no citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, language, or any of them. The opening non-obstante clause of Article 15(4)—'Nothing in this article or in clause (2) of article 29 shall prevent the State from making any special provision...'—specifically creates an exception to Article 29(2). This ensures that reserving seats, waiving fees, or lowering admission criteria for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Socially and Educationally Backward Classes in government or state-aided institutions cannot be challenged as prohibited caste-based discrimination under Article 29(2).
questions.explanation_hindi: अनुच्छेद 15(4) भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 29(2) के साथ घनिष्ठ संबंध में कार्य करता है। अनुच्छेद 29(2) प्रत्येक नागरिक को यह मौलिक गारंटी देता है कि राज्य द्वारा पोषित या राज्य निधि से सहायता प्राप्त किसी भी शैक्षणिक संस्थान में प्रवेश से केवल धर्म, मूलवंश, जाति, भाषा या इनमें से किसी के आधार पर वंचित नहीं किया जाएगा। अनुच्छेद 15(4) की शुरुआत एक गैर-अवरोधक खंड (non-obstante clause) से होती है: 'इस अनुच्छेद की या अनुच्छेद 29 के खंड (2) की कोई बात राज्य को... विशेष उपबंध करने से निवारित नहीं करेगी'। यह उपबंध अनुच्छेद 29(2) के सामान्य गैर-भेदभाव नियम का एक प्रत्यक्ष संवैधानिक अपवाद निर्मित करता है, जिससे राज्य द्वारा संचालित या सहायता प्राप्त स्कूलों और कॉलेजों में SC, ST और SEBC के लिए सीटों का आरक्षण अनुच्छेद 29(2) का उल्लंघन नहीं माना जाता।

questions.question_english: Article 46 of the Constitution of India, which directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, is enshrined in which Part of the Constitution?
options_english: Part III (Fundamental Rights)
Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy)
Part IVA (Fundamental Duties)
Part IX (The Panchayats and Local Governance)
questions.explanation_english:
Article 46 of the Constitution of India is located within Part IV of the Constitution, which encompasses the Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36 to 51).

Constitutional Framework of Part IV:
1. Non-Justiciability: Under Article 37, the provisions contained in Part IV are not enforceable by any court (non-justiciable through judicial writs). However, Article 37 explicitly affirms that 'the principles therein laid down are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.'
2. Role in Social Welfare: Article 46 serves as a foundational constitutional compass directing executive policy, welfare schemes, educational budgets, and affirmative social action for weaker sections, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes across both central and state education ministries.
questions.explanation_hindi:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 46 संविधान के 'भाग IV' में स्थित है, जिसमें राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व (अनुच्छेद 36 से 51) शामिल हैं।

भाग IV का संवैधानिक ढांचा:
1. गैर-न्यायसंगतता (Non-justiciability): अनुच्छेद 37 के अनुसार, भाग IV के प्रावधान किसी भी न्यायालय द्वारा लागू नहीं कराए जा सकते (अर्थात इनके उल्लंघन पर रिट जारी नहीं की जा सकती)। हालांकि, अनुच्छेद 37 यह स्पष्ट करता है कि ये सिद्धांत 'देश के शासन में मूलभूत हैं और विधि बनाने में इन सिद्धांतों को लागू करना राज्य का कर्तव्य होगा।'
2. सामाजिक कल्याण में भूमिका: अनुच्छेद 46 केंद्र और राज्य सरकारों के लिए एक मार्गदर्शक का कार्य करता है, जो कमजोर वर्गों, अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के कल्याण, छात्रवृत्तियों, छात्रावासों और शैक्षिक बजट के निर्माण में नीतिगत आधार प्रदान करता है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Part IV (Directive Principles)

questions.explanation_english:
The Constitution (One Hundred and Third Amendment) Act, 2019, which came into effect on 14 January 2019, amended Articles 15 and 16 of the Constitution of India by inserting two new clauses:

1. Article 15(6): Empowers the State to make special provisions for the advancement of any economically weaker sections of citizens (other than the classes mentioned in clauses (4) and (5)), including up to 10% reservation in admission to educational institutions, whether aided or unaided, excluding minority educational institutions referred to in Article 30(1).

2. Article 16(6): Empowers the State to provide up to 10% reservation in public employment and appointments for economically weaker sections of citizens other than the classes mentioned in clause (4).

Note: Article 15(5) was inserted earlier by the 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2005 (for OBC/SC/ST reservations in educational institutions), whereas Article 16(5) existed originally in the Constitution (relating to religious offices).

questions.explanation_english: In landmark rulings beginning with M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore (1963) and reaffirmed by the 9-judge Constitution Bench in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), the Supreme Court held that reservations under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) should generally not exceed 50%. The Court reasoned that Article 15(4) is an enabling special provision, and if reservations were permitted to swallow the majority of seats (such as 60%), the overarching guarantee of equality of opportunity and merit under Article 15(1) and Article 29(2) would be rendered meaningless. While extraordinary situations in far-flung, remote regions might justify a deviation, the standard constitutional cap on reservations in educational institutions remains capped at 50%.

Legal and Policy Rationale:
1. Absolute Prohibition: The law strictly bars financial transactions or monetary payouts as the foundation of conciliation to prevent wealthy or influential perpetrators from buying off complainants or monetizing workplace sexual harassment.
2. Mandatory Duty of ICC: When any monetary offer is made by the respondent or demanded during conciliation, the ICC is statutorily bound to inform both parties that financial settlements are impermissible under the Act and refuse to record or facilitate any such arrangement.
3. Permissible Terms: Conciliation may include apologies, reprimands, behavioral undertakings, or changes in supervisory/reporting arrangements.
4. Default to Inquiry: If the parties cannot reach an agreement on lawful, non-monetary terms, the ICC must terminate conciliation and proceed with a regular inquiry under Section 11.

Therefore, option (C) is the legally mandated procedure.
